text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finnish printing houses' exports to Russia are still growing but stabilizing after last four years of rapid growth.
- Finns would prefer slightly a left-centre-goverment over the current "rainbow" coalition after 1999 parliamentary elections, poll shows.
- Employees' work burden should be lightened and brought into the focus of next pay deal negotiations, says Seppo Junttila of Confederation of Salaried Employees (STTK). @
- Government underestimates minorities' rights in Finland and majority of population's racist opinions are worrying, says International Helsinki Federation in latest human rights report.
- Excavation of vast northern theme park, Santaworld, has began and park in caves is scheduled to open in autumn 1998; Santaworld will become as popular as Disneyland, builders say.
- International analysts expect Raisio to increase earnings per share by four or five times after deal with U.S group Johnson&Johnson oto market cholesterol-cutting Benecol agent in United States. @

- In June, GSM mobile phones were sold at record speed and demand is still increasing strongly; one in three Finns has a portable phone, globally more than in any other country, sector representatives say.
- Skilled construction workers are scarce, but shortage of labour is not yet a bottleneck to strongly recovering construction sector, deputy director at building firm NCC-Puolimatka says. @

- European Union's regional subsidies for agriculture will be restructured and Finnish farmers' subsidies may be cut by 500 million markka, European Commission's enlargening report to Eastern Europe, Agenda 2000 shows.
- Small- and middle-sized chemicals companies improved profitability clearly last year, sector study shows.
